Polished UI with dark theme

No tasks tracked yet.

Typecheck clean. The polish is delivered through design tokens, which propagate across every page already using semantic colors (Weekend Hub, Sessions, Tyres, Setup, Pitwall, AI Engineer, Debrief, Engineering Memory):

  • Darker, denser dark theme — near-black background, technical hairline borders, tighter radius (0.375rem) and smaller body type (14px / 1.5) for the MoTeC-style information density.
  • Faint shadows, subtle inset top highlights — no SaaS drop shadows.
  • New utilities for direct use in any component: .tech-panel + .tech-panel-header (with accent bar), .data-table (compact, sticky header, tabular-nums, row hover), .kpi-stat (channel-value style), .section-eyebrow, .grid-backdrop, and a .status-dot.live for live indicators.
  • Mono everywhere defaults to tabular numerics.

Routes unchanged; six-section nav untouched.

can all the calender entrys send a reminder on the device and on race week end can it send a reminder/alarm 30min befor the session start

Added reminders to calendar

No tasks tracked yet.

Done. Reminders are wired up:

  • Calendar entries — On /calendar, click the new Reminders button to enable browser notifications and pick lead times (defaults: 1 day + 1 hour before).
  • Race-weekend sessions — Any session in your active weekend triggers an alarm 30 min before start (configurable: 5/10/15/30/60 min).
  • Notifications are de-duped so they don't refire on reloads, and the button shows how many alerts are currently scheduled.

One honest caveat: browser notifications only fire while the app is open in a tab. For true background push (closed tab / phone locked) we'd need to set up Web Push with a service worker — say the word if you want me to add that next.

go for it

I'll add background push via a service worker so reminders fire even when the tab is closed/phone is locked. Quick approach: extend the existing /sw.js to handle scheduled local alerts via the Notification Triggers API where available, and use showNotification from the SW (which works when the page isn't focused). True web push needs a push server (VAPID + subscriptions) — I'll wire that up too using a server function to store subscriptions, but actual push delivery requires a backend cron. Let me start with the most reliable wins first.
